Opens 2nd Saturday in September, 9 days. Draw only — no OTC.
5 days, opens first Wednesday after Oct 8. Elk-primary, limited/draw.
9 days, deer + elk combined. OTC in many units.
9 days, deer + elk combined. OTC in many units.
5 days, combined. Draw only.
28-day fixed September rifle season.
Concurrent with archery elk.
Concurrent with muzzleloader deer/elk.
Runs with the four combined deer/elk rifle seasons.

points.summary: Highest points draw first — a straight line, not a lottery. You earn one point for each year you apply unsuccessfully, or by submitting a point-only application. Points zero out when you draw your FIRST-CHOICE hunt code. Second, third, and fourth choices do not use your points, so you can chase a low-demand backup without burning your stack.
rules: Points apply to your first choice only. Later choices are effectively a random leftover draw.
Drawing your first choice resets that species' points to zero. Drawing a 2nd–4th choice does NOT burn points.
A point-only application costs the application fee and banks a point without any chance of drawing.
Hunt codes that take 6+ points for residents cap nonresidents at 20% of licenses; everything else allows up to 25%.
You must hold a qualifying license (small game or equivalent) to apply.
Bear, pronghorn, elk, and deer each track points separately.

units.name: GMU 74
units.desc: La Plata & San Juan counties. Core Durango-area unit north and east of town — Hermosa Creek country, Missionary Ridge, upper Animas drainages.

units.name: GMU 75
units.desc: La Plata & San Juan counties. Heavy San Juan NF timber, Vallecito and Pine River drainages, Weminuche Wilderness edge.

units.name: GMU 751
units.desc: Paired with 75, generally the lower-elevation and more private-land-influenced portion. Popular DIY unit.

units.name: GMU 77
units.desc: Piedra River country between Durango and Pagosa Springs.

units.name: GMU 771
units.desc: Adjacent to 77, lower country toward Chimney Rock and the Piedra confluence.

units.name: GMU 78
units.desc: East of the Piedra toward Pagosa Springs and the Navajo River.

units.name: GMU 781
units.desc: Adjacent to 78, toward the New Mexico line.

units.name: GMU 73
units.desc: Northwest of Durango toward Rico and the Dolores River.

units.name: GMU 80
units.desc: Open sage and pinyon-juniper country west of Durango — primary pronghorn ground in the Four Corners region.

units.name: GMU 81
units.desc: Adjacent to 80, similar open country. Limited pronghorn draw.

waters.name: Animas River
waters.note: Gold Medal water through town. Browns and rainbows. Runoff typically blows it out May–June.

waters.name: Vallecito Reservoir & Creek
waters.note: Kokanee, northern pike, browns, rainbows. Inlet fishes well in fall.

waters.name: Lemon Reservoir / Florida River
waters.note: Close to Durango, stocked rainbows, some browns below the dam.

waters.name: Piedra River
waters.note: Wild browns and rainbows in a rugged canyon. Access via First Fork and Piedra Rd.

waters.name: Navajo Reservoir / San Juan (CO side)
waters.note: Warmwater and trout mix; the famous San Juan quality water is below the dam in New Mexico.

waters.name: Weminuche high lakes
waters.note: Cutthroat and brookies, ice-off through September.

seasons.note: Archery period precedes the rifle season in most areas. Requires archery permit.
Typical general-license rifle window in Areas 10, 13, 15, 21. Antlerless extension Nov 1–7 in several areas.
Longer general window close to Laramie. Limited-quota Type 1 also available.
Large limited-quota Type 1 allocation. Type 2 antlered (5 points or less) Nov 21 – Dec 31.
Area-specific antlerless and private-land seasons. Check the area listing.
Archery period runs ahead of the rifle opener; exact dates vary by hunt area.
All Wyoming pronghorn is limited quota. Dates and quotas are set per hunt area.
Mortality-quota driven — areas close mid-season when the female quota is hit. Call the hotline before you go.
Same quota-closure system. Baiting legal in Wyoming with restrictions.

points.type: Preference points — nonresident only for elk/deer/pronghorn
points.summary: Wyoming splits limited-quota nonresident licenses 75/25: three quarters go to the preference-point draw (highest points first) and one quarter to a pure random draw, so a zero-point applicant always has a shot. Residents do NOT use preference points for elk, deer, or pronghorn — resident draws are fully random.
rules: 75% of nonresident limited-quota licenses go to the point draw; 25% are random.
Drawing your first-choice license zeroes your points for that species.
Miss applying AND miss buying a point for two consecutive years and you lose that species' points entirely.
You can buy points July 1 – November 2 without holding a hunting license.
Special vs. regular draw: paying the higher 'special' license price puts you in a separate, usually shallower, applicant pool.
Residents: elk, deer, and pronghorn limited quota are random — no points to build.

units.name: Elk Area 6 — Pole Mountain
units.desc: Immediately east of Laramie between US 30/287 and I-25 to the Colorado line. General plus limited Type 1 (50), Type 4 antlerless (25), and unlimited Type 8 cow/calf off national forest.

units.name: Elk Area 7 — Laramie Peak
units.desc: Large area from Glenrock south and west. Big limited-quota allocation: Type 1 (1,500), Type 2 antlered 5-point-or-less (350), Type 6 cow/calf (2,000), Type 8 private-land cow/calf.

units.name: Elk Area 8 — Boulder Ridge
units.desc: South of Laramie between US 287 and WY 10. Type 1 limited (150) plus unlimited Type 8 cow/calf. Long Oct 1 – Jan 31 rifle window.

units.name: Elk Area 10 — Rock Creek
units.desc: West of Laramie along WY 130 to the Laramie/Medicine Bow river divide. General license area — rifle Oct 15–31, antlerless Nov 1–7. Type 6 cow/calf (300).

units.name: Elk Area 13 — Encampment River
units.desc: Continental Divide at the Colorado line north to WY 70. General license — archery Sep 1–30, rifle Oct 15–31, antlerless Nov 1–7. Type 6 cow/calf (150).

units.name: Elk Area 15 — Spring Creek
units.desc: Sage Creek Rd (CR 401) at the Divide north to the North Platte. General license, same Oct 15–31 rifle window. Type 6 cow/calf (200).

units.name: Elk Area 16 — Shirley Mountain
units.desc: Between Laramie Peak and Shirley Ridge, I-80 at the North Platte to WY 220. All limited quota — Types 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 with staggered Oct–Jan windows.

units.name: Elk Area 21 — Baggs
units.desc: WY 789 at the Colorado line north to Muddy Creek. Sierra Madre elk herd. General license — rifle Oct 15–31, youth-only Oct 11–12. Type 6 cow/calf (200).

waters.name: North Platte River — Encampment to Saratoga
waters.note: Blue-ribbon brown and rainbow water. Treasure Island, Bennett Peak, and the Miracle Mile upstream. Best after runoff drops, late June onward.

waters.name: Encampment River
waters.note: Wilderness canyon section above town holds wild browns and brookies. Steep access.

waters.name: Snowy Range alpine lakes (Libby, Lewis, Marie, Mirror)
waters.note: Brookies, cutthroat, splake, golden trout in select lakes. WY 130 closes in winter — typically open late May/June through October.

waters.name: Laramie River
waters.note: Browns and rainbows; much of the good water is private, check WGFD walk-in and HMA access.

waters.name: Lake Hattie / Twin Buttes
waters.note: West of Laramie. Rainbows, browns, and kokanee. Wind is the deciding factor.

waters.name: Medicine Bow River
waters.note: Browns in the upper reaches near the Snowies; warms up considerably downstream.
